question: Pan-retinal photocoagulation (PRP) laser is indicated for proliferative diabetic retinopathy and works by destroying ischaemic peripheral retina to reduce VEGF production.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. PRP laser destroys ischaemic retina, reducing VEGF production and causing new vessel regression. It is the standard treatment for PDR. The trade-off is peripheral and night vision loss.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. PRP destroys the hypoxic peripheral retina that is driving VEGF production. This reduces the stimulus for neovascularisation and causes regression of new vessels. It sacrifices peripheral vision to protect central vision.
